name: mcp
description: The MCP endpoint over a listening server, with the official MCP client (@modelcontextprotocol/client): initialize, tools/list and tools/call through the HTTP runtime's gate and the engine's access policy, a refused call as a tool error carrying the problem document, an unknown tool as a JSON-RPC error, the 2026-07-28 revision beside the 2025 ones, the behavior catalog's tools, service callers, and the core's behaviors' operations as tools. The HTTP API and the MCP endpoint are mounted on one app. On Node.js the server is @hono/node-server, on Bun it is Bun.serve.
omitted: the core's behaviors > Constants and Variants add no tool: create's data and update's patch show each variant, and a result in the wrong shape and a changed kind are tool errors with the 422 problem
the core's behaviors > Dependencies and Links are tools: create takes their parameters, listLinked takes no id; a gated transition and a required target's delete are tool errors with the 409 problem
the core's behaviors > Rollups adds a field and no tool: get carries the rollups' values, computed at the read, and a gated transition is a tool error with the 409 problem

tools.name: list_schemas
tools.title: List schemas
tools.description: Lists the schemas this namespace reaches, its own and the shared namespace's, with each one's live version and whether it has a draft.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn which schemas this namespace reaches and which of them have a live version.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's fields or operations; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each schema's name, its live version and whether it has a draft.

tools.name: describe_schema
tools.title: Describe a schema
tools.description: Returns a schema's describe document: how a UI shows an instance (its display, and each field's title and icon), the JSON Schema of an instance, the behaviors its type composes with their config, and every operation with its parameters, its result and its tool.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before calling a schema's tools: it gives the JSON Schema of an instance, each behavior with its config and summary, and each operation with its parameters, result and guidance.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read instances; call the schema's get or list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the describe document of the live version.

tools.name: define_schema
tools.title: Define a schema draft
tools.description: Stores a schema-file document (the form superschematic format --to=json writes) as the draft of its name, replacing the draft before it. It does not publish: a draft goes live only through the HTTP publish route.

document.description: The schema-file document: kind General, a name, and the types; superschematic format --to=json writes it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to store a schema-file document as the draft of its name, replacing the draft before it.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to publish: a draft goes live only through the HTTP publish route.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the draft, with its name and hash; the live version is unchanged.

tools.name: list_behaviors
tools.title: List behaviors
tools.description: Lists the behaviors this engine runs, which a schema's types may compose: each one's name and description, the behaviors it requires and conflicts with, and the fields and operations it adds.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before composing behaviors in a draft, to learn which behaviors this engine runs.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's config of its behaviors; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each behavior's name, description, requirements, conflicts, fields and operations.

tools.name: describe_behavior
tools.title: Describe a behavior
tools.description: Returns a behavior's declaration: the JSON Schema of the config a type gives it, of the parameters a create gives it and of the entry a write's preconditions carry for it, the behaviors it requires and conflicts with, its fields, its operations with their scope, parameters, result and invocation policy, and the codes its vetoes carry.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn what a behavior takes before composing it: its config, its create parameters, its preconditions and the codes its vetoes carry.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's config of the behavior; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the behavior's declaration, with its defaults filled in.

tools.name: get_value
tools.title: Get a stored value
tools.description: Returns a value the engine stores by its hash, { hash, bytes, value }: a field whose JSON is longer than the engine's threshold, which an event (and an instance read with valueRefs) carries as a ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }. The caller must be able to read a schema of this namespace whose instances, events or behaviors hold the value.

hash.description: The value's hash: the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON, as a ref's $value holds it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read a large field an event, or an instance read with valueRefs, carries as a ref ({ "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }), by its hash.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read an instance; call its schema's get, which returns every field inline unless valueRefs asks for refs.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the value with its hash and its size in bytes.

tools.name: list_namespaces
tools.title: List namespaces
tools.description: Lists the namespaces the caller may see: each one's name, whether the engine's options configure it or a create made it, whether it is the shared namespace, and whether it is archived.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn which namespaces you may see, and whether each is archived.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to list a namespace's schemas; call list_schemas.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each namespace's name, origin (configured by the engine's options, or created), whether it is the shared namespace, and its state (active or archived).

tools.name: create_namespace
tools.title: Create a namespace
tools.description: Creates a namespace, which holds schemas and instances of its own and looks schema names up in the shared namespace after itself. Its name is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to make a namespace for a new project: it starts with no schemas of its own and looks schema names up in the shared namespace after itself.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to make a schema; call define_schema in the namespace. Do not use for a name that is a namespace already, archived or not: the create is refused (conflict).
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, active, with who made it and when.

tools.name: archive_namespace
tools.title: Archive a namespace
tools.description: Archives a namespace a create made: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, and it refuses every write, and runs no reaction or schedule, until it is unarchived.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when a project made with create_namespace is finished: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, every write is refused (namespace_archived), and its reactions and schedules stop.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on a namespace the engine's options configure, which is refused (conflict), or to remove data: nothing is removed.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, archived, with who archived it and when; archiving an archived namespace changes nothing.

tools.name: unarchive_namespace
tools.title: Unarchive a namespace
tools.description: Lets an archived namespace be written again; its reactions and schedules pick up where they stopped.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to write again to an archived namespace.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on an active namespace, which stays as it is.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, active; its reactions and schedules pick up where they stopped.

tools.name: item_create
tools.title: Create Item
tools.description: Creates a Item: validates the instance, data, against the schema's live version and stores it under id, or under a new id when none is given.

id.description: The instance id; the engine makes one when it is absent

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to create a new Item: data holds its own fields, and id names it, or the engine makes one.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change one that exists; call update.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the new instance with its id, its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

tools.name: item_get
tools.title: Get Item
tools.description: Returns the Item with the id: its own fields in data, its behaviors' in behaviors.

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when you have the id of the Item to read.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to find Item instances; call list.

tools.name: item_list
tools.title: List Item
tools.description: Lists Item instances in creation order, a page at a time: pass a page's next as cursor for the page after it. where keeps the instances whose fields hold the values it gives, a list meaning any of them; a filtered page can hold fewer than limit while next is not null.

limit.description: How many instances a page holds, 50 when absent

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

where.description: The values the instances hold, by field: a value, null for none, or a list of 1 to 100 meaning any of them; every member must hold

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to page through Item instances, oldest first. where keeps the ones whose fields hold the values it gives, null meaning no value and a list of values any of them: title; a behavior's field by its qualified name, the behavior's, a dot and the field's.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read one instance whose id you have; call get.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null. With where, a page can hold fewer items than limit, even none, while next is not null: read on until it is.

tools.name: item_update
tools.title: Update Item
tools.description: Applies a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) to the Item with the id: a member replaces the instance's, a nested object merges and null removes a member. With expectedSeq the update is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

patch.description: A JSON merge patch of the Item

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to change the own fields of the Item with the id, as a JSON merge patch; with expectedSeq, the update is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to set a behavior's field: the patch holds own fields only, and a behavior's fields change only through its operations.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance as the patch left it, with its next seq.

tools.name: item_delete
tools.title: Delete Item
tools.description: Deletes the Item with the id. With expectedSeq the delete is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to delete the Item with the id for good; with expectedSeq, the delete is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns null; the instance and what its behaviors kept for it are gone.

s30.description: Creates a namespace, which holds schemas and instances of its own and looks schema names up in the shared namespace after itself. Its name is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

s31.name: archive_namespace
s31.title: Archive a namespace
s31.description: Archives a namespace a create made: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, and it refuses every write, and runs no reaction or schedule, until it is unarchived.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when a project made with create_namespace is finished: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, every write is refused (namespace_archived), and its reactions and schedules stop.

superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, archived, with who archived it and when; archiving an archived namespace changes nothing.

s32.name: unarchive_namespace
s32.title: Unarchive a namespace
s32.description: Lets an archived namespace be written again; its reactions and schedules pick up where they stopped.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to write again to an archived namespace.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on an active namespace, which stays as it is.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before calling a schema's tools: it gives the JSON Schema of an instance, each behavior with its config and summary, and each operation with its parameters, result and guidance.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read instances; call the schema's get or list.

tools.name: define_schema
tools.title: Define a schema draft

document.description: The schema-file document: kind General, a name, and the types; superschematic format --to=json writes it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to store a schema-file document as the draft of its name, replacing the draft before it.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to publish: a draft goes live only through the HTTP publish route.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the draft, with its name and hash; the live version is unchanged.

tools.name: list_behaviors

tools.description: Lists the behaviors this engine runs, which a schema's types may compose: each one's name and description, the behaviors it requires and conflicts with, and the fields and operations it adds.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before composing behaviors in a draft, to learn which behaviors this engine runs.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's config of its behaviors; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each behavior's name, description, requirements, conflicts, fields and operations.

tools.name: describe_behavior
tools.title: Describe a behavior
tools.description: Returns a behavior's declaration: the JSON Schema of the config a type gives it, of the parameters a create gives it and of the entry a write's preconditions carry for it, the behaviors it requires and conflicts with, its fields, its operations with their scope, parameters, result and invocation policy, and the codes its vetoes carry.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn what a behavior takes before composing it: its config, its create parameters, its preconditions and the codes its vetoes carry.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read a schema's config of the behavior; call describe_schema.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the behavior's declaration, with its defaults filled in.

tools.name: get_value
tools.title: Get a stored value
tools.description: Returns a value the engine stores by its hash, { hash, bytes, value }: a field whose JSON is longer than the engine's threshold, which an event (and an instance read with valueRefs) carries as a ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }. The caller must be able to read a schema of this namespace whose instances, events or behaviors hold the value.

hash.description: The value's hash: the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON, as a ref's $value holds it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to read a large field an event, or an instance read with valueRefs, carries as a ref ({ "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }), by its hash.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read an instance; call its schema's get, which returns every field inline unless valueRefs asks for refs.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the value with its hash and its size in bytes.

tools.name: list_namespaces
tools.title: List namespaces
tools.description: Lists the namespaces the caller may see: each one's name, whether the engine's options configure it or a create made it, whether it is the shared namespace, and whether it is archived.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to learn which namespaces you may see, and whether each is archived.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to list a namespace's schemas; call list_schemas.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns each namespace's name, origin (configured by the engine's options, or created), whether it is the shared namespace, and its state (active or archived).

tools.name: create_namespace
tools.title: Create a namespace
tools.description: Creates a namespace, which holds schemas and instances of its own and looks schema names up in the shared namespace after itself. Its name is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to make a namespace for a new project: it starts with no schemas of its own and looks schema names up in the shared namespace after itself.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to make a schema; call define_schema in the namespace. Do not use for a name that is a namespace already, archived or not: the create is refused (conflict).
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, active, with who made it and when.

tools.name: archive_namespace
tools.title: Archive a namespace
tools.description: Archives a namespace a create made: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, and it refuses every write, and runs no reaction or schedule, until it is unarchived.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when a project made with create_namespace is finished: its schemas, instances and events stay readable, every write is refused (namespace_archived), and its reactions and schedules stop.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on a namespace the engine's options configure, which is refused (conflict), or to remove data: nothing is removed.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, archived, with who archived it and when; archiving an archived namespace changes nothing.

tools.name: unarchive_namespace
tools.title: Unarchive a namespace
tools.description: Lets an archived namespace be written again; its reactions and schedules pick up where they stopped.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to write again to an archived namespace.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on an active namespace, which stays as it is.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the namespace, active; its reactions and schedules pick up where they stopped.

A change of the instance's own fields consumes every gate's sign-offs, unless the config keeps them, and entering a gated state consumes that gate's, so a return to it signs again. expect.name: Constants
expect.description: Fields of the type that its create sets and nothing changes after: an update that changes one, a caller's or one a behavior's operation applies, is refused at the field, unless the caller holds the config's permission. A field the create leaves absent stays absent. What routes an instance, such as a step's kind or the key a blueprint stamped it with, stays what its create gave it.

expect.name: Dependencies
expect.description: Blockers between instances. A blocker is finished once its status is a terminal state of its own schema's Workflow whose outcome the config accepts, a success by default. An instance is blocked while a blocker is not finished, and a transition of its own Workflow into a gated state waits until none blocks it. A blocker is an instance of the type's own schema, or of a schema the config lists, that composes Workflow; an edge that would close a cycle is refused. A create may give its blockers. Deleting a blocker removes its edges.

expect.name: Derived
expect.description: Own fields a model outside the engine fills from other own fields, under an instruction the schema holds (D73). The engine calls no model: a deriver holding the config's permission pulls the stale fields with staleDerivations (each one's inputs, instruction, model label and the field's JSON Schema, which is the output's) and settles its answers with settleDerivations, presenting the hash it pulled. A value is written with the operation's update(), so the type's validation and every guard judge it, and its event attributes it to Derived with the confidence given. A field is stale when its inputs, instruction, model or type moved since its last value; that value stays until a new one settles. Once a caller, or another behavior's operation, writes a derived field, Derived stops deriving it until rederive. A failure appends no event; after maxAttempts the field waits until its inputs move. Deleting the instance deletes what Derived keeps of it.

expect.name: Links
expect.description: Named links from the instance to instances of the schemas its config names, set by link or given at create: each holds one target, or with many a list of them. A pinned link records the target's revision (its schema composes Revisions) or its release (its schema composes Branches), and reports the target's latest beside it and whether the target has moved past it. A required link is given at create, can be moved to another target but not unlinked, and the delete of its target is refused; a required many-valued link keeps at least one target, and only its last target's delete is refused. A deleted target leaves every link that holds it.

expect.name: Numbering
expect.description: A number a person reads on each instance, set in its create's transaction from a count per namespace and schema: the format prints it, INV-{yyyy}-{seq:4} as INV-2026-0042. The count may run per target of a required, single-valued link and start again each UTC year, so a label is unique within its scope. A refused create takes no number; a delete leaves a gap. Nothing changes a number once set, and a list finds an instance by its label or its number. An instance made before its schema composed Numbering is numbered by assignNumber.

expect.name: Provenance
expect.description: Who set each own field last, and through what (D73): a caller's create or update, or the behavior whose operation wrote it, with the confidence that operation attributed (D16, amended). With review, a write from the sources it names is proposed until a reviewer holding its permission accepts or rejects it, unless its confidence reaches below; a caller's write over a proposal makes it edited. A gate refuses a move of the type's Workflow into its state while a field it lists is proposed. Deleting the instance deletes its records.

expect.name: Reactions
expect.description: Rules that move Workflow statuses after a change commits: when the instance's status enters a state, when a field of the instance, its own or a behavior's, changes, when every instance that links to it through a link is in a terminal state, optionally one with a listed outcome, when one of them enters a terminal state with a listed outcome, when an all or any rollup of the instance comes to hold, or when the instance one of its links points to gains a revision or a release, move the instance, or the instance one of its links points to, to a state. An engine runs them after the commit, as the principal it names for its runner, so a rule never refuses the change that set it off. A target already in the state, with no transition to it, or whose guards refuse is left as it is.

expect.name: Revisions
expect.description: Immutable revisions of the instance's own fields: one when it is created and one each time they change, numbered 1, 2, 3, ..., read a page at a time or one by its number. With review in its config, a caller can propose a change as a merge patch, citing instances as evidence, and a caller who holds the review permission approves it, which applies the patch as an update, or rejects it; pendingProposals counts the proposals waiting. Deleting the instance deletes its revisions and proposals.

A value is computed when the instance is read, as the caller, from at most 500 linked instances; a rollup over more has none. A rollup of every or some one may gate states of the type's Workflow: a transition into one waits until the rollup holds.

expect.name: Search
expect.description: Full-text search over the instance's own text fields, which the config names, and with vectors in the config, vector search over embeddings an outside embedder computes from the same text. The index is kept in the transaction of each create, update and delete; an embedder pulls the instances whose text changed since their vector was computed (staleEmbeddings) and settles their vectors back (settleEmbeddings). The schema-level search returns the matching ids in rank order, by the text, by a vector the caller gives, or by both fused, from the instances of the caller's namespace only, and similar returns the instances nearest to one, or to a draft's text.

A field is held when it is neither absent nor null. A transition into a state while a field it requires is not held is vetoed, and a create whose initial state requires one is refused at the field. An update, a caller's or one a behavior's operation applies, that clears a field the instance's state requires, or changes one it freezes, is vetoed; a caller with the config's permission may change a frozen field. tools.name: search
tools.title: Search every schema
tools.description: Searches the instances of every schema this namespace reaches that composes Search and that the caller may read, and returns one ranking: by query, by vector (with its model), or both. Each hit names its schema and says how it matched. Before creating an instance, search for its text to find near-duplicates.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

model.description: The model the vector was computed with; required with a vector.

query.description: What to search for, as text.

syntax.description: How to read the query: words (the default), each word as text, or fts5, an SQLite FTS5 expression.

vector.description: The vector to search for, computed with model: it ranks the schemas whose vectors come from that model, with as many dimensions.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to find instances across every schema this namespace reaches that composes Search, by words, by a vector, or both.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to page through one schema's instances; call its list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns hits best first, each naming its schema and how it matched, and next for the page after.

tools.name: notes_create
tools.title: Create notes
tools.description: Creates a notes: validates the instance, data, against the schema's live version and stores it under id, or under a new id when none is given.

id.description: The instance id; the engine makes one when it is absent

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to create a new Note: data holds its own fields, and id names it, or the engine makes one.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change one that exists; call update. Do not create a duplicate: call similar with the draft's text first, to find one to reuse.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the new instance with its id, its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

tools.name: notes_get
tools.title: Get notes
tools.description: Returns the notes with the id: its own fields in data, its behaviors' in behaviors.

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use when you have the id of the Note to read.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to find Note instances; call list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance with its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

tools.name: notes_list
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: Lists notes instances in creation order, a page at a time: pass a page's next as cursor for the page after it. where keeps the instances whose fields hold the values it gives, a list meaning any of them; a filtered page can hold fewer than limit while next is not null.

limit.description: How many instances a page holds, 50 when absent

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

where.description: The values the instances hold, by field: a value, null for none, or a list of 1 to 100 meaning any of them; every member must hold

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to page through Note instances, oldest first. where keeps the ones whose fields hold the values it gives, null meaning no value and a list of values any of them: title or body; a behavior's field by its qualified name, the behavior's, a dot and the field's.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read one instance whose id you have; call get.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null. With where, a page can hold fewer items than limit, even none, while next is not null: read on until it is.

tools.name: notes_update
tools.title: Update notes
tools.description: Applies a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) to the notes with the id: a member replaces the instance's, a nested object merges and null removes a member. With expectedSeq the update is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

patch.description: A JSON merge patch of the Note

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to change the own fields of the Note with the id, as a JSON merge patch; with expectedSeq, the update is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to set a behavior's field: the patch holds own fields only, and a behavior's fields change only through its operations.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the instance as the patch left it, with its next seq.

tools.name: notes_delete
tools.title: Delete notes
tools.description: Deletes the notes with the id. With expectedSeq the delete is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to delete the Note with the id for good; with expectedSeq, the delete is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns null; the instance and what its behaviors kept for it are gone.

tools.name: notes_search
tools.title: notes: search
tools.description: Searches the schema's instances in the caller's namespace and returns the matching ids, best match first, one page at a time: by query, by vector, or by both, whose rankings are fused. A query is plain words by default: an instance matches when its indexed fields hold every word, and quotes and operators in the query are text. With syntax fts5 the query is an SQLite FTS5 expression (phrases, AND, OR, NOT, NEAR, prefix*), without column filters. A vector, computed with the config's model from the text to search for, ranks the instances whose vectors are settled by cosine similarity. With a vector, each hit says how it matched.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

model.description: The model the vector was computed with; refused when it is not the config's.

query.description: What to search for, as text.

syntax.description: How to read the query: words (the default), each word as text, or fts5, an SQLite FTS5 expression.

vector.description: The vector to search for: as many numbers as the config's dimensions, computed with its model.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use to find Note instances by words in title or body: plain words match when the fields hold every one; syntax fts5 takes an FTS5 expression. A vector of 384 numbers from model minilm-l6 ranks by similarity, alone or fused with a query.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to page through every instance; call list.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns hits best first, each its id, rank and a snippet of the field that matched. Pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: notes_similar
tools.title: notes: similar
tools.description: Lists the instances nearest to an existing one, leaving it out: by its own indexed text and, once its vector is settled, by its vector, the two rankings fused, each hit saying how it matched. Given text in place of an id, the text of an instance not yet created, it ranks the same way by that text and the vector given with it, if any. Call it before creating an instance, to find near-duplicates to reuse or link instead.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

id.description: The instance whose neighbours to list.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

model.description: The model the vector was computed with; refused when it is not the config's.

text.description: In place of id, the text of an instance not yet created: its indexed fields that hold more than whitespace, in the config's order, joined by a blank line, as an embedder is given an instance's.

vector.description: With text, the text's vector: as many numbers as the config's dimensions, computed with its model.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use before creating a Note, to find near-duplicates to reuse or link instead: with id, the instances nearest to one you have; with text, the ones nearest to a draft's title and body, joined by a blank line. With text, a vector of 384 numbers from model minilm-l6 computed from the same text ranks by similarity too.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to search by a few words; call search.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the nearest instances, leaving out the one named by id, and whether a vector ranked (embedded). Pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: notes_stale_embeddings
tools.title: notes: staleEmbeddings
tools.description: Lists the instances whose vector is missing or stale, in the order they were first indexed: each one's id, the text to compute its vector from (its indexed fields, joined by a blank line) and the hash of that text and the model, which a settle presents. Needs vectors in the config.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many instances; 50 when absent.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use as an embedder: it lists the instances whose vector from minilm-l6 is missing or stale, with the text to embed and its hash.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns the model, the dimensions and the items. Pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null.

tools.name: notes_settle_embeddings
tools.title: notes: settleEmbeddings
tools.description: Stores the vectors an embedder computed from the text staleEmbeddings returned, each with the hash it returned with it. An item whose instance is gone, or whose text or model changed since, is skipped. A vector of the wrong dimensions, all zeros, or with a value a 32-bit float cannot hold refuses the whole batch. Needs vectors in the config and the permission it names. Appends no event: a vector is derived from text the log records, and no read of an instance shows it.

sourceHash.description: The hash staleEmbeddings returned with the text.

superschematic/operation-guidance.useWhen: Use as an embedder with permission notes.embed: it stores at most 100 vectors of 384 numbers, each with the hash staleEmbeddings gave.
superschematic/operation-guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not settle a vector computed from other text or another model: its hash no longer matches and it is skipped.
superschematic/operation-guidance.success: Returns how many it settled and each skipped item with its reason, moved or not_found.
